prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: Japanese Lighthouse catalog design candidate LH07-0068 履歴と分類を備えたページ移動パレット.
Reference hierarchy: ORIGINAL source image(s) control icon glyph geometry, proportions, optical/stroke weight, alignment, spacing and fine control anatomy. Our saved FigCraft mock is secondary for Japanese content and overall layout; do not copy its rough substitute icons or omissions. Official Lighthouse white/forest-green/slate design and locked Japanese typography remain binding.
Input images: Image 1: original-source-reference. Image 2: enlarged-original-palette-detail. Image 3: secondary-component-preview. Image 4: approved-style-reference. The final approved bus style image controls only surface/gradient craft, never content or unrelated icons.
Render ONE compact page-navigation palette, intended420x458 logical px instead of552x654. White card, fine neutral outline, radius8, tiny soft shadow on pure white canvas. Search row32 high, three group headings18 high each, twelve item rows28 high each, footer28 high. Side padding12 and icon/text gap8. ALL text Meiryo Regular, no bold. Search and item labels14px/24; headings, shortcut and footer12px/16. Exact text/order: search ページを検索; heading 操作; item 組織を切り替え with right18px keycap 組. Heading 最近使ったページ with small history-clock icon; three items 指標 — 確認 / 監視 — 確認と問題 / 外部連携 — 作成. Heading すべてのページ; eight items 作成ツール / アシスタント / チーム / ツール / 電話番号 / 認証キー / 音声ライブラリ / ワークフロー. Restore original16px slate icons for each item: switch opposite horizontal arrows; line chart with axes; thermometer; diagonal linked plugs; two crossed ellipse atom; person bust; three people; wrench; telephone handset; padlock; five vertical audio bars; branching three circular nodes. Match original fine stroke/proportion. Do not copy repeated document substitutes. NO selected row or invented green action. Footer separated by hairline, exact ↑ ↓ で移動 / 改行キーで選択 / 組織を切り替え / 14件; put existing up/down arrows in tiny separate keycaps and add source return-arrow keycap before Japanese selection label, and Japanese組 keycap before footer switch label, preserving all21 existing text blocks. Count14 right aligned, complete footer fits420width without shrinking12px. No extra hidden rows, no source English category suffixes beyond authored Japanese strings. Small white outer margin; preserve normal font roles while compressing rows/padding.
Official constraints: pure #FFFFFF outer canvas; Do not invent an outer card around a flat component. Only existing card surfaces use rounded corners, fine neutral outlines and soft downward shadows; flat headings, lists and settings stay flat white. Primary actions use smooth #174C36 → #1F6444 → #2D8F5E gradient with legible white glyphs/labels and restrained edge light. Ordinary supporting icons #526173 unless a specifically justified group/state overrides. No broad mint, decorative multicolored icons, excessive gloss or invented data/features. Preserve exact Japanese text and existing Meiryo typography, weights, line heights and wrapping. Orthographic clean UI render, no phone/environment, no watermark.
Accent decision: White palette, thin neutral border, small8corners and weak shadow. Coherent slate icons and charcoal labels, gray metadata, quiet individual keycaps; no added forest row or broad tint.
LATEST DIRECT OWNER DENSITY CORRECTION, 2026-10-18: previous candidates were too big and too spacious. This overrides earlier source-spacing and presentation-enlargement instructions. Use compact ordinary UI proportions, content-driven control widths, restrained small radii, tight but readable padding, and little outer presentation whitespace. Preserve exact established Japanese font roles; do not shrink text to manufacture density. Preserve original icon geometry, strokes, states and artwork. Avoid stretching a small standalone utility control across an entire screen. Use the owner-corrected180x28 three-segment control as a density reference only, not a size to force onto unrelated components. Output image pixels are inspection resolution, never intended application CSS size.
